question.prompt: What is the value of the following expression? \[\dfrac{\frac{3}{8}+\frac{7}{8}}{\frac{4}{5}}\]

solutions.explanation:
The long fraction bar divides the entire numerator by \(4/5\), so first add the fractions on top. Their denominators are equal:
\[
\frac38+\frac78=\frac{10}{8}=\frac54.
\]
Dividing by the nonzero fraction \(4/5\) means multiplying by its reciprocal, \(5/4\). Thus
\[
\frac54\div\frac45
=\frac54\times\frac54
=\frac{25}{16}.
\]
The value is \(\frac{25}{16}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Add first, then divide
